description:
Macklin Celebrini delivered a sensational sophomore season, establishing himself as a budding superstar. He became just the sixth player in NHL history to reach 100 points as a teenager and was electric every time he touched the puck. Finishing fourth overall in league scoring, Celebrini tallied 45 goals and 70 assists for 115 points, outpacing his next closest Sharks teammate by a staggering 56 points.  
One of his standout moments came against in-state rival Los Angeles. With the Sharks trailing late and their goalie pulled for the extra attacker, Celebrini danced through two Kings defenders with dazzling skill before firing home the game-tying goal.  
Against Dallas, he showcased his elite playmaking ability. Off an offensive zone faceoff, Celebrini used a clever trick move to push the puck forward and catch the Stars off guard. Maintaining control, he waited patiently until a seam opened cross-ice, then delivered a perfect pass to a wide-open Collin Graf in front for the Sharks goal.  
Finally, against Calgary, Celebrini scored an incredible spin-o-rama goal — the eventual game-winner — that left Sharks fans in awe of his creativity and skill.

description:
In the 2007 Stanley Cup Playoffs, Scott Niedermayer — the veteran defenseman and leader for the Anaheim Ducks — delivered an incredible performance that earned him the Conn Smythe Trophy and his 4th Stanley Cup championship.
Featured in this highlight are three standout moments that defined his dominance: Niedermayer’s spectacular 2OT series clincher in Game 5 of the first round, where he fired a shot from the blue line to advance the Ducks with unforgettable drama. Then, his clutch overtime goal in Game 2 of the Western Conference Final against Detroit to even the series and keep the championship dream alive. And his dramatic game-tying goal with under a minute left in Game 5 of the Western Conference Final, forcing overtime and refusing to let the series slip away.
Niedermayer’s clutch plays anchored the Ducks’ run to the Cup, showcasing the two-way excellence that made him playoff MVP.

description:
In the first period against the Carolina Hurricanes, Tim Stützle — the dynamic star forward for the Ottawa Senators — authored a highlight-reel goal that instantly entered the conversation as a potential goal-of-the-year candidate.  
Intercepting a pass at the blue line in his own defensive zone, Stützle turned defense into pure offense with explosive speed, bursting up the ice on a breakaway while weaving past pursuing defenders. Closing in on the net, he sold a slick deke that froze the goaltender before finishing with a backhand shot that beat the outstretched pad and gave Ottawa a 2-1 lead.  
Stützle’s incredible individual brilliance shifted the momentum in a high-scoring affair and stood out as one of the most dazzling plays of the entire season. The Senators would go on to defeat the Hurricanes 6-3.

description:
In Game 6 of the Western Conference First Round, Quinn Hughes — the star defenseman acquired by the Minnesota Wild in a blockbuster midseason trade — delivered a dazzling two-goal performance that carried his team to its first playoff series victory in 11 years.  
Hughes opened the scoring in the first period with a snipe that ignited the home crowd and set the tone. But it was his second goal midway through the third period that stood out as the series-clincher. With the score tied, the dynamic blueliner ripped a pinpoint wrist shot from the left dot that banked in off a skate and beat the goaltender to break the deadlock and put Minnesota ahead for good.  
Hughes’ clutch three-point night sparked a 5-2 victory that eliminated the Dallas Stars in six games and propelled the Wild into the second round.

description:
Cole Caufield reached a landmark 50th goal of the 2025-26 season, becoming the first Montreal Canadiens player to hit the milestone since Stephane Richer in 1989-90.
Midway through the second period, Caufield drove down the right wing on a rush, took a precise feed from Nick Suzuki, and wired a clean wrist shot from the circle past the goaltender to open the scoring. The Bell Centre erupted in a lengthy standing ovation as the sniper celebrated the historic tally on home ice. 
The goal highlighted a career year in which Caufield finished with 51 goals overall and led the entire NHL with 12 game-winning goals. His ability to deliver in clutch moments and light the lamp with elite shot accuracy cemented his status as one of the League’s premier pure goal scorers while helping power Montreal’s strong campaign.

description:
In a matchup against the New Jersey Devils, Anze Kopitar — the legendary center and face of the Los Angeles Kings franchise — produced a two-goal game that saw him surpass Marcel Dionne for the most points in franchise history.
His second goal of the game made for the milestone moment as he snapped a shot from low in the right face-off circle to tie the game at 4-4 and reach 1,308 career points. description:
Matthew Schaefer capped a historic 2025-26 rookie season by capturing the Calder Memorial Trophy as NHL Rookie of the Year. The 18-year-old first-overall pick finished with 23 goals and 59 points, tying the single-season record for goals by a rookie defenseman while leading all first-year players in ice time and becoming the youngest unanimous Calder winner in League history. 
In his home debut, Schaefer scored his first NHL goal, diving into a net-front scramble on the power play and poking the puck home to give Islanders fans their first lasting memory of the franchise cornerstone. Weeks later, he became the youngest player in NHL history to score a regular-season overtime goal, ripping a one-timer from the right circle off a short feed to secure a hard-fought victory. 
The highlight of his skill arrived midseason when Schaefer exploded through the neutral zone, danced around multiple defenders with elite speed and edge work, and finished a dazzling individual rush to tie the game—showcasing the dynamic, high-end talent that defined his breakthrough year. 
Schaefer’s combination of offensive creativity, heavy minutes, and two-way maturity announced the arrival of a generational blueliner and set the foundation for a bright new era on Long Island.

description:
Dale Hawerchuk began his storied NHL career with the Winnipeg Jets, delivering an extraordinary rookie season that earned him the Calder Trophy after racking up 103 points, including 45 goals. A Hockey Hall of Fame inductee in 2001, Hawerchuk remains a legend of the game.

description:
Guy Lafleur was the electrifying engine of the Montreal Canadiens’ high-powered offense in the 1970s, thrilling fans with his speed, flair, and lethal scoring ability. A five-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner, he became the first player in NHL history to record six straight seasons with 50 goals and 100 points. With his flowing hair and smooth stride, Lafleur became a beloved icon in Montreal and a Hockey Hall of Famer. 

Among his many clutch goals, perhaps the most iconic was his game-tying blast in Game 7 of the 1979 Semifinals against the rival Boston Bruins. With the Canadiens on a late power play and trailing by one, Lafleur led the rush up ice, dished the puck forward, then trailed the play to rip a one-timer off a drop pass that beat the goalie and sent the home crowd into a frenzy. Montreal would go on to win the game in overtime on Yvon Lambert’s goal and later defeat the New York Rangers in the Final to claim their fourth straight Stanley Cup.

description:
In 1994, Mark Messier delivered one of the most iconic performances in NHL history, backing up a bold promise with a clutch Game 6 effort that kept the New York Rangers’ season alive. With the team trailing the New Jersey Devils 3–2 in the Eastern Conference Final, Messier famously declared, “I know we’re going to go in and win Game 6 and bring it back here for Game 7,” according to the New York Daily News. He then made good on his guarantee by scoring a natural hat trick in the third period, leading the Rangers to a 4–2 comeback victory and forcing a decisive Game 7.  
Down 2–1 entering the third period, Messier took control. He tied the game early in the period on the backhand, gave the Rangers the lead driving the net on a rebound, and sealed the game—and his guarantee—with a shorthanded, empty-net goal. That final goal was especially memorable: it began with Messier winning a defensive-zone faceoff during a 6-on-4 penalty kill, then skating up ice to finish the play into the vacant net.    
The Rangers would go on to win Game 7 in double overtime against the Devils and eventually defeat the Vancouver Canucks in the Stanley Cup Final, ending a 54-year championship drought. Messier’s Game 6 performance remains one of the most clutch and iconic moments in NHL playoff history.

description:
Game 7 of the 2001 Stanley Cup Final. On home ice with the Stanley Cup within reach, captain Joe Sakic steps up and delivers the moment Avalanche fans will never forget. Early in the second period, Colorado’s on the power play against the New Jersey Devils when Sakic takes the puck along the right wall in the offensive zone. With Martin Brodeur locked in net, Sakic freezes the defense with a slap shot fake, then steps inside the faceoff circle and snaps a perfect shot upstairs, roofing it over Brodeur’s glove.  
The goal gave Colorado full control of the game and set them on their way to hoisting the Stanley Cup. It was Sakic’s 13th goal of the playoffs, capping off a dominant postseason where he also led all players with 26 points. After a Hart Trophy season, Sakic’s clutch finish was the ultimate captain’s moment, sealing his legacy with a championship-winning dagger.

description:
Brendan Shanahan joined the New York Rangers for the 2006–07 season, bringing a powerful presence and scoring touch to a team with playoff aspirations. On opening night, Oct. 5, 2006, Shanahan made an immediate impact, scoring twice in a 5–2 win over the Washington Capitals. His first goal gave the Rangers a 3–1 lead and stood as the game-winner. His second goal, early in the third period during a delayed penalty, marked a major milestone—his 600th career goal—making him just the 15th player in NHL history to reach that mark. A three-time Stanley Cup champion and one of the preeminent power forwards of his era, Shanahan played over 1,500 NHL games and finished his career with 656 goals and 1,354 points. He spent two seasons in New York before returning to the New Jersey Devils, the team that originally drafted him, for the final year of his Hall of Fame career.

description:
Jordan Staal capped a legendary 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs by capturing the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP. The Hurricanes captain scored eight goals in the postseason, including a historic six in the Final against Vegas — becoming the first player in more than 50 years to score in each of the first five games of a Stanley Cup Final and just the second team captain in 105 years to reach six goals in the series.

In Game 2, Staal delivered a crucial third-period goal that helped fuel Carolina’s resilience. In Game 4, he scored twice, with his second of the night — a desperate, swat of the puck from in tight — proving to be the game-winner and producing one of the series’ most iconic moments. In Game 5, he tied the game with a first-period tip-in, continuing his streak. 

Beyond the goals, Staal dominated the faceoff circle throughout the Final, winning 68 percent of his draws (83 wins against just 39 losses) while matching up against Vegas’ top centers and anchoring a lockdown defensive effort. The veteran’s combination of clutch scoring, leadership, and two-way excellence powered Carolina to its first championship since 2006 and cemented his place in franchise lore.

description:
In a matchup against the Vegas Golden Knights, Logan Cooley — the rising star center for the Utah Mammoth — put on a career performance with a 5-point night that left fans in awe.
Cooley tallied four goals, including a backbreaking tally in the third period after forcing a turnover, and added an assist to power the Mammoth to a 5-1 victory. The young phenom notched his first 4-goal game and first 5-point game in the NHL, showcasing the elite skill and finishing ability that have made him one of the league’s most exciting young talents.
Cooley’s explosive display highlighted his breakout season and gave fans a glimpse of the superstar potential that continues to electrify the game.

description:
In the third period of Game 2 against the Boston Bruins, Erik Karlsson — the dynamic defenseman and offensive wizard for the Ottawa Senators — produced an incredible assist that tied the game and shifted the momentum in the series.
With the score 3-2 late in regulation, Karlsson took the puck and took the Bruins for a skate, dazzling defenders with his elite skating and stickhandling before delivering a perfect feed to Derick Brassard for the tying goal.
Karlsson’s highlight-reel assist sparked Ottawa’s comeback in an overtime victory that prevented the Bruins from taking a 2-0 series lead and the Senators losing the first two games at home. Ottawa would go on to close out the series in six games, with Karlsson’s magic helping set the tone for one of the most memorable playoff runs in franchise history. Despite not playing in the Stanley Cup Final (the team lost in the Eastern Conference Final), Karlsson led all NHL defensemen in assists (16) and points (18) during the 2017 Stanley Cup Playoffs.

description:
Mitch Marner opened Game 6 of the Second Round with a sensational between-the-legs goal that set the tone for Vegas’ series-clinching victory.  
Just 1:02 into the contest, Marner took a stretch pass from William Karlsson, drove hard toward the net, and absorbed contact from a closing defender. Fighting through the pressure, he hit the brakes, turned, and slipped the puck between his own legs past the goaltender to give the Golden Knights a 1-0 lead.  
The dazzling opener was signature Marner magic. He later added an assist on the shorthanded series-clinching goal as Vegas advanced with a dominant win.  
Marner finished the 2026 postseason leading the entire NHL with 29 points in 22 games while posting a plus 11 rating.
